tagline: Verified JVC G24 TV quirks and firmware-scoped capability data
description: JVC G24 TV / SW8_JVC_NZ, Android 11. Records the physical panel, app display modes, 1080p graphics composition, HDR UI driver limitation, observed audio behavior, remote Settings key and buffer tests. Recommends Android-window UI buffers on the tested firmware. Unknown limits stay unknown; connected receiver support is not a TV-wide codec guarantee.
capabilities: Shares the digital tuner across Antenna, Cable, and Satellite where applicable
Enables the manual TV backlight control in Control Centre when permission is available
Provides display, sound, OS, remote and buffer facts to Eclipse
Firmware-scoped rendering recommendations; user choices take precedence
Preserves unknowns and distinguishes advertised support from verified operation

capabilitySections.title: Device and firmware
items: JVC G24 TV, product SW8_JVC_NZ, Android 11 (API 30).
The measurements below are from firmware RTM9.241015.070, security patch 2024-12-01; other firmware may behave differently.
Manufacturer: skyworth; board: anaheim. Supported ABIs: armeabi-v7a and armeabi.

capabilitySections.title: Inputs
items: Android reported four HDMI passthrough inputs and one composite passthrough input.
Antenna, Cable and Satellite can share the TV's digital tuner.
Input settle delays: HDMI 2.2 seconds; tuner 1.5 seconds.
One concurrent TV preview was observed as safe. The number of TV input scalers is unknown.
HDMI snapshot capture is unknown and requires a consented test with non-protected content.

capabilitySections.title: Display
items: Physical panel: 3840 x 2160. Android reported 1920 x 1080 app display modes at 50 Hz and 60 Hz.
Panel HDR types reported by Android: Dolby Vision, HDR10 and HLG. Panel HDR support does not establish HDR interface output.
The observed graphics composition target was 1920 x 1080. Tested 4K UI buffers were composed into that target before scaling to the panel.
Graphics: ARM Mali-G52 r25p1-01bet0; OpenGL ES 3.2.
JVC picture backlight control supports 0-100 in steps of 5; manual mode and WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission are required.

capabilitySections.title: Sound
items: PCM and eARC return audio were observed in the tested setup. PCM worked with the tested external receiver; bitstream behaviour depends on the connected audio route.
The audio policy advertised AAC, AC-3, AC-4, E-AC-3, E-AC-3 JOC and PCM formats; advertised formats are not proof of playback.
The built-in speaker report includes two channels and sample rates from 8 kHz to 192 kHz; codec and channel limits remain unknown.
The later audio policy report did not show an eARC policy entry. This does not negate the separately observed return-audio result.

capabilitySections.title: Remote control
items: The plugin adds KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION (83) as a Settings shortcut.
Android reported navigation, Select, Back, Home, Settings, Notification, TV Input and Volume keys present. Key presence does not prove Eclipse receives them.
Firmware may intercept input keys; use Eclipse button mapping to test delivery.

capabilitySections.title: Buffers and video
items: UI buffer sizes tested: 1920 x 1080 and 3840 x 2160, in RGBA_8888 format.
HDR UI output was not supported in the tested driver; floating-point EGL format was advertised but BT.2020 PQ EGL colour space was not.
Native-resolution UI buffers measured about 18.8 frames per second in the recorded test; an observed 1080p interface output measured about 60 frames per second.

Android reported video decoder types including AV1, AVC, HEVC, Dolby Vision, MPEG-2, VP8 and VP9. Reported decoder counts, dimensions and frame rates require validation and are not guarantees of simultaneous playback.
An intermittent frozen or black thumbnail was observed during libVLC fullscreen-to-Home surface handoff.

capabilitySections.title: Verification and recommendations
items: Measurements used Android APIs and read-only local ADB. Raw diagnostics were not included.
Eclipse recommends Android-window UI buffers on this firmware instead of native-resolution buffers; explicit user choices take precedence.
Audio encoding override: unknown. Connected receiver support is not a TV-wide codec guarantee.
App display mode is not a measurement of frame rate. HDR video support is not evidence of HDR UI output.
